solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ability to decide if rib is broken inside body cavity

indicators.note: a thing placed inside goes within another, so one string is set into the middle of a longer one

parts.note: an atrium is a chamber of the heart or another body cavity

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so its letters can be put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor wonders whether a cracked rib lodged in the chest affects a patient's judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body cavity' sounds anatomical alongside rib, but the cavity is a heart chamber; the scrambled letters slip in after its opening letter. 'If' and 'is' only join the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitrium is the Latin-derived term for free will or the power of deciding, as in liberum arbitrium.

clue.text: More than one clover leaf ultimately detached from breast pads worn by Kelvin

indicators.note: clothing worn by someone sits around them, so one piece wraps round another
something detached is separated and taken away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: falsies are pads worn to make the bust look bigger

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of leaf
K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: A strange sartorial scene: someone named Kelvin wearing padded underwear with a clover leaf falling off it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove F from FALSIES to leave ALSIES, then K slips inside: ALSI-K-ES. Kelvin looks like a man's name but is the scientific unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsike is a species of clover grown for fodder, so the plural form names several such plants.

clue.text: The people addressed in dialect to support British subsidiary

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
ye is the old or regional word for you, the people being spoken to

explanation.surface: A dialect speaker is urged to back a British firm's subsidiary company.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, a piece that supports another sits underneath it, so YE goes below B.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, bye (also spelt by) means secondary or incidental, as in a by-road or bye-law.

clue.text: Type of net containing one live Canadian lake fish

indicators.note: to contain something is to hold it within, so the first piece surrounds the rest

parts.note: tulle is a fine silk or nylon netting
the Roman numeral for one
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A fishing net holds a single live fish caught in a Canadian lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'net containing live fish' sounds like angling, but the net is a fabric, and the inserted letters sit before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: The tullibee is a whitefish or cisco found in the Great Lakes and other lakes of Canada.

clue.text: A flat piece cut from young sheep's feet

indicators.note: trimming the horizontal stroke off a letter changes its shape into a different letter

parts.note: lambs are young sheep

explanation.surface: A butcher slices a flat cut of lamb from its trotters.
explanation.walkthrough: Draw a capital L and cut off its flat base stroke: what remains is an I, so LAMBS becomes IAMBS.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a foot is a metrical unit, and the iamb, an unstressed then stressed syllable, is the commonest kind.

clue.text: Commend hot seaside walk northward to do with a dreamy god?

definitions.text: to do with a dreamy god?

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading from the bottom up, against the usual direction

parts.note: to cite someone is to commend them officially, as in a military citation
H for hot, as on a tap
short for promenade, the walkway along a seafront

explanation.surface: Someone praises a warm stroll along the seafront heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string of three pieces is read upwards. The question mark flags that the definition is playful: the dreamy god is Morpheus.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphetic means relating to Morpheus, the Greek god of dreams, so it describes anything belonging to that deity.

clue.text: Respected Muslim woman to have an adhesive effect?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a title of honour for a Muslim lady of rank in South Asia
second meaning, split in two: to be glue-like stuff, that is, to be a sticky resin

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is BE GUM: to be gum is to stick. The question mark warns that this second meaning is a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Begum is an honorific used in Pakistan, India and Bangladesh for a married or high-ranking Muslim lady.

clue.text: Not quite reasonable to stop Cricket Club festival in Pakistan

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so one piece is pushed into the middle of another

parts.note: a cricket club is a bat, the implement used to strike the ball

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: sane means reasonable or sensible

explanation.surface: Someone argues it is not fair to cancel a cricket club's festival in Pakistan.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make Cricket Club look like an organisation; it is just the club a batsman swings in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Basant is the spring kite-flying festival celebrated in Lahore and elsewhere in Punjab.

clue.text: Relating to fine-grained rock, right to replace both uranium in fertiliser and sulphur in medicine

indicators.note: to replace something is to take its place, and 'both' means one swap-in letter does the job twice

parts.note: guano is bird or bat droppings used as fertiliser
R is the abbreviation for right
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
physic is an old word for medicine
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A geological instruction about chemicals in fertiliser and medicine reads like a lab recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: One R swaps for the U in GUANO and the same R swaps for the S in PHYSIC, giving GRANO and PHYRIC. 'Both' tells you one R does both jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Granophyre is a fine-grained igneous rock with intergrown quartz and feldspar; the adjectival form describes its texture.

clue.text: Magnetic unit is the greatest thing by a considerable margin

parts.note: the max is the maximum, the greatest amount
as in well ahead, meaning by a long way

explanation.surface: A boast that some magnet is far and away the best thing around.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first and 'is' joins it to two plain pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The maxwell is the CGS unit of magnetic flux, named after the physicist James Clerk Maxwell.

clue.text: Scottish rogue's year away from largest Inner Hebridean isles, one of them to the west

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west means moving leftwards, against the reading direction
something away from a place is gone from it, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: Skye and Mull are the two biggest islands of the Inner Hebrides
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A Scottish scoundrel spends a year away from the islands, sailing off westward.
explanation.walkthrough: SKYE loses its Y to give SKE, and only MULL, 'one of them', heads west to become LLUM. The definition carries 's, read as 'is', so it joins to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Skellum is a Scots and Dutch-derived word for a scoundrel or good-for-nothing, a straight synonym for a rogue.

clue.text: Backgrounds of lacemakers bringing Marine uniform into King

indicators.note: bringing something into a place carries it inside, so one piece is put within another

parts.note: rex is Latin for king, used in royal signatures
marine means of the sea
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lace workshop dresses a Royal Marine in uniform for the King's visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Marine and King look like a soldier and a monarch; uniform looks like dress but is a NATO alphabet letter. Rex is the Latin royal signature.
explanation.definitionFit: A réseau is the plain net ground on which a lace pattern is worked; the French plural ends in X.

clue.text: Pan for preparing balti somewhat lackadaisically

indicators.note: somewhat means to some degree, so only part of the following word is used

parts.note: the letters run inside the middle of the adverb

explanation.surface: Someone cooks a curry in a half-hearted, lazy way.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in lac-KADAI-sically. 'Somewhat lackadaisically' reads as an adverb for the cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A kadai, also karahi, is the deep two-handled metal pan in which balti curries are cooked and served.

clue.text: Parasitic worm has topsy-turvy eccentric, complete drunkard, losing both feet

indicators.note: topsy-turvy means upside down, which in a down entry flips the order of letters

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person

indicators.note: in a down entry the foot of a word is its bottom letter, and losing it removes the end

parts.note: uncut means complete or unabridged
lush is slang for a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A worm infects an upside-down oddball and a total alcoholic who has lost both feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Both UNCUT and LUSH drop their last letter, giving UNCU and LUS; 'both feet' means one foot each.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracunculus is the genus of the Guinea worm, a nematode parasite that lives under human skin.

clue.text: Special layer completed elliptical auditorium

parts.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
a hen is a bird that lays eggs, a layer
done means finished or completed

explanation.surface: Builders finish a special stratum of a curved theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' reads as a stratum but means something that lays, here a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphendone is the curved or elliptical end of an ancient stadium or theatre, or a sling-shaped auditorium.

clue.text: Adoration of serpents or pike put back in fancy tanks

indicators.note: something put back goes the other way round, so its letters run in the opposite direction
in places one thing within another, so one piece is set inside the rest
fancy means elaborate or ornamented, signalling letters dressed up in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
luce is an old name for a pike, especially a full-grown one

explanation.surface: Someone worships snakes, or else keeps a pike in an ornamental aquarium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy tanks' reads as decorative fish tanks, which suits a pike, but fancy is the signal to rearrange. Luce is an old word a solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A cult is a system of religious worship, so a snake cult is the worship of serpents as sacred.

clue.text: University and Bern, somehow united with Slough, touch wood in Thuringia

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged in an unstated order

parts.note: taken as written
U for united, as in football club names
a slough is a bog or marsh, as is a fen

explanation.surface: A university in Bern merges with the English town of Slough while someone crosses fingers in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is an English town, but here it is the common noun meaning a swamp. 'In Thuringia' signals a German answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unberufen is the German exclamation used, like knocking on wood, to ward off bad luck after a boast.

clue.text: Barrel-shaped drum to carry with the backpiece foremost

indicators.note: putting the rear part at the front moves the final letter round to the start

parts.note: to hold something is to carry it

explanation.surface: A drummer carries a big drum with its back panel facing forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The final D of HOLD moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The dhol is a large double-headed barrel drum from the Indian subcontinent, played at bhangra performances.

clue.text: When to turn and drive on slimy sediment

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
to propel is to drive forward

explanation.surface: Advice on when to turn a car and keep going on a muddy surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' and 'drive' read as motoring instructions; 'on' places the first piece above the second in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapropel is the dark, organic-rich ooze that settles on the bottom of lakes and seas, a kind of slimy mud.

clue.text: Showy young man seen in skinsuits oddly cut

indicators.note: removing the odd-numbered positions leaves just the second, fourth and every other even letter

parts.note: the even letters of the word, once the first, third and so on are gone

explanation.surface: A flashy young man shows up wearing tight bodysuits with odd cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly cut' looks like a description of the skinsuits' tailoring but tells you to cut the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Knut is an Edwardian slang term for a dandy or fashionable young man about town.

clue.text: Finisher left Kath unoccupied on Australian co-operative farm

parts.note: a KO, or knockout, finishes a boxing bout
L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: an unoccupied space has nothing in its middle, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name
Oz is informal for Australia or Australian

explanation.surface: A woman called Kath leaves an Australian farm empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three pieces sit on OZ in the down entry. Kath reads as a person but is just letter fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A kolkhoz was a collective farm in the Soviet Union, worked co-operatively by its members.

clue.text: Males harbouring a younger love for Western cowboys

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter within, so the outer piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: bucks are male deer, rabbits or similar animals
taken as written
YR is an abbreviation for younger
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Some men are sheltering a youthful sweetheart from the Wild West ranch hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Younger love' reads as a young sweetheart, but it is two abbreviations, and love is the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckayro is a variant spelling of buckaroo, the American word for a cowboy, from Spanish vaquero.

clue.text: Uptake of light food brought about peculiar swellings

indicators.note: to bring something about another is to put it around it, so one piece encloses the other
taking something up in a down entry lifts it bottom to top, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: eats is informal for snacks or light food
rum means odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: Taking in some snacks caused strange lumps to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uptake' reads as eating, but in a down entry it means lifting letters bottom to top. Rum meaning odd is everyday British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Struma is a medical term for a goitre or a scrofulous swelling; strumae is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Cunning old senior barrister retained by American being sent up

indicators.note: sending something up in a down entry makes it read from the bottom, against the usual order
something retained by another is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Yank is informal for an American
King's Counsel, the title for senior barristers in the reigns of past kings

explanation.surface: A crafty veteran lawyer is kept on by an American who is being mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' looks like mockery but means turned upside down. 'Old' is there because KC applies under a king, and for decades the title was QC.
explanation.definitionFit: Knacky is a dialect word meaning clever, ingenious or crafty, someone with a knack for things.

clue.text: Huge number of rupees for some, one individual's number in coffers

parts.words: Huge number of rupees for some
parts.note: a lac or lakh is one hundred thousand, used for rupees in South Asia
'un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good 'un'
an aria is a solo song in an opera, one singer's number

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs a fortune in rupees and their own number into treasure chests.
explanation.walkthrough: Coffers reads as money chests but here means the sunken panels of a ceiling. 'For some' tells you only some people count in lacs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacunaria are the recessed panels in a ceiling or vault, which architects also call coffers.

clue.text: A large eucalyptus perhaps, or red sandalwood probably

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
eucalyptus trees are called gum trees, so a eucalyptus is an example of a gum

explanation.surface: A botanist guesses at a timber: a big eucalyptus, or maybe red sandalwood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks eucalyptus as an example of a gum tree. 'Probably' in the definition reflects scholarly uncertainty about the biblical tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Algum is the biblical timber Solomon imported, which scholars think was likely red sandalwood from India.

clue.text: Elaborate fugue without care for instrument in Tanglewood's kitchen section?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: a ricercare is an elaborate contrapuntal piece, an early form of fugue
taken as written

explanation.surface: An orchestral player tackles a complex fugue carelessly, on an instrument from the orchestra's kitchen department.
explanation.walkthrough: Tanglewood is a famous summer music festival, so 'instrument' and 'section' sound orchestral; the question mark flags that it is a kitchen gadget instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricer is a kitchen utensil that presses cooked potato through small holes, so it is a culinary tool.

clue.text: Wingers from Arsenal Football Club advanced, following behind Henry in preparation for a softer kick?

indicators.note: behind sets the long run of wordplay after the single letter, so the short piece leads

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so the two edge letters are taken

parts.note: the first and last letters of the club name
FC is the standard abbreviation for Football Club
A for advanced, as in A level
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Football talk: Arsenal's wide men push forward behind Thierry Henry, setting up a gentler shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry suggests the Arsenal striker Thierry Henry, but here it is the unit. Everything else comes 'behind' H. The kick is caffeine, not a football kick.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-caf coffee mixes regular and decaffeinated beans, so the drink gives a milder caffeine jolt.

clue.text: Become almost sinless in the morning tower before temple

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to go can mean to become, as in 'go mad'
pure means free from sin
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A devotee nearly becomes free of sin through early morning prayer at the temple.
explanation.walkthrough: PURE drops its E to give PUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A gopuram is the tall ornamented gateway tower at the entrance of a South Indian Hindu temple.

clue.text: Notes about singular legal matter

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale and also means about, so it serves both words
S is the abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A lawyer's memo notes points about a single legal issue.
explanation.walkthrough: RE means about in business letters, and S follows it. 'Notes' also hints at the whole answer, since res is the plural of the note re.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, res is Latin for a thing or matter, as in res judicata, a case already decided.

clue.text: Centred slices from razor get pen nice and sharp

indicators.note: slices from the centre are cut out of the middle of each word, leaving the core letter

parts.note: the centre letters of each of the two words
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A writer claims a razor-sliced nib makes a fountain pen nicely sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: Razor and get each have one centre letter, Z and E. 'Pen' looks like a writing tool but is an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Zesty means piquant and pleasantly tangy, a flavour that is both agreeable and sharp.

clue.text: Quickness of Spenser's finish for Epithalamion: one's damned short

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter is dropped
the finish of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the poem's title
read as 'I'm', one is
blessed is a mild ironic oath meaning damned, as in 'not a blessed thing'

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at the brief ending of Spenser's wedding poem Epithalamion.
explanation.walkthrough: Epithalamion is Spenser's marriage ode, so it fits the surface. BLESSED loses its D. 'One's' becomes I'M because a speaker calls themself I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimblesse is the Spenserian noun for nimbleness, so it names speed and agility in that poet's language.
